claim: A levered/diversified 60/40 portfolio scaled to match the S&P 500's own volatility level outperformed the S&P 500 (12.5% vs 9.2% annualized in the modern period shown, at nearly identical ~14-15% volatility), illustrating that the value of diversification has to be judged against a volatility-matched (levered or delevered) version of the concentrated alternative, not against the concentrated portfolio at its own natural risk level.
quote: This allowed us to match the risk level of equities and benefit from the enhanced risk-efficiency of the diversified portfolio.
limitations: Practitioner blog post, not peer reviewed; illustrative 60/40-vs-equities example, not a study of ETF-rotation sleeve combinations specifically; historical US 1962-2017 sample, no cost/tax treatment matching our next-open 10/20bp contract.
independent_replication: The underlying mechanism (volatility/leverage matching for fair comparison) is the same principle documented formally in AQR's 'Understanding Risk Parity' and 'Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity' (Asness, Frazzini, Pedersen), which this round's external-brief.json also cites.
impact_on_spec: Sets the preregistered comparison: each sleeve mix is judged against S3 scaled to the same realized volatility (k*S3 + (1-k)*SHY per window), so the mix is credited only for diversification beyond plain de-risking.
